newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek short rates ease, all eyes on FRN tender.
newsitem.headline: Greek short rates ease, all eyes on FRN tender.

text.p: Greek short-run interbank depos and forex forwards were softer, ecu/drachma was firmer and bonds were frozen as the market awaited the result of today's auction of seven-year floaters, dealers said.
"Short-term depos and forex forwards have fallen due to improved liquidity conditions," said a senior dealer at a private bank. "The market focuses on today's FRN auction."

Implied drachma rates from forex forwards were hovering around 11.65 percent in periods up to two months, 11.45 percent in three-months, 10.85 percent in nine-months and 10.55 in one-year, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Fixed coupon bonds and floaters were paralysed awaiting the outcome of the FRN auction today.
"The bond market is frozen awaiting the outcome of the FRN auction," said a senior dealer at a private bank. "The range of accepted bids might be wide but we will see some clustering around par."
Greece auctioned 150 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs today. The first coupon has been set at 10.40 percent.
The results of the auction are expected later on.
The ecu continued to strenghten against the drachma breaking out of its weak resistance at 310 temporarily before receding around 309.90/95.

"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.60 and hit an intraday high of 310.05/10 before receding to 309.90/95 after the fixing," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The central bank seems to be indifferent at these levels and ecu/drachma is directionless, driven by small amounts."
Ecu buying for drachmas from local players accounted for the drachma's weakness, said a dealer.
"If ecu/drachma breaks the 310 resistance, we are heading for higher levels," he said. "The next resistance is 310.50."
The mark was quoted at 157.97/07 from Thursday's 158.110 fix, the dollar at 272.91/01 drachmas from 272.780 and the ecu at 309.84/94 from 309.940 drachmas.
